tagline: The city below, and cable cars on the hill.
intro: Along Grandview Avenue on Mount Washington, downtown Pittsburgh spreads below the byway. McArdle Roadway and Sycamore Street are also part of the route. Nearby inclines climb the steep hillside where workers settled in the 1860s, when industry had taken the flat land along the river.

The Monongahela and Duquesne inclines are the two survivors of seventeen that once carried passengers in the city. At the western end of the byway, a bronze George Washington meets the Seneca leader Guyasuta face to face, their weapons down.

moments.title: Monongahela Incline
moments.text: The passenger incline climbs Mount Washington on a line designed by John Endres with help from his daughter Caroline.

moments.title: Duquesne Incline
moments.text: Restored cars show their original wood as the incline climbs toward an observation deck overlooking the Golden Triangle.

moments.title: Point of View Park
moments.text: At Grandview Avenue and Sweetbriar Street, a bronze meeting between Washington and Guyasuta occupies the edge of Mount Washington.
